slice_id: intraday P19 market-calendar-aware cash-flow contribution timing

phase0_history.design: naive addition of one SkipCashFlow override per non-trading day (up to ~150-200/year) to the existing per-tick due() call
phase0_history.finding: 1 Major -- RecurringCashFlowSchedule._recurrences re-walks from occurrence index 0 on every due() call regardless of window start, and per-tick calling combined with the ~150-200x override multiplier produces a benchmarked 6.3x slowdown, extrapolating to tens of minutes to hours for a realistic full-year backtest. 2 Minor (inherited DST risk on new target dates unstated; empty-tape test's call-site update unmentioned), 1 Nit

phase0_history.design: gate due() on calendar-date equality (self._cash_flow_window_date) -- call at most once per calendar day instead of once per tick
phase0_history.verdict: GO (0C/0M/2m/1N) then rejected before any code landed
phase0_history.finding: rejected not by a reviewer but by the opus BUILDER's own cold probing before writing any tests: the calendar-date gate assumed a day's first tick always arrives at or after that day's scheduled contribution instant (the anchor's time-of-day). False whenever a later trading day's session starts earlier in local time than the anchor day's own time-of-day (pre-market data differing across days, or a mid-session tape start) -- probed concretely, could silently lose a day's contribution entirely if that day was also the tape's last day. Also found a documentation gap: the ADR required the existing test suite stay unedited, but ADR-0176's own window-advancement test pins the exact behavior this change deliberately alters.

phase0_history.design: gate due() on the next unconsumed SCHEDULED FUNDING INSTANT (a precomputed sorted list of exact epoch-ms values plus an advancing index pointer) instead of calendar-date equality
phase0_history.finding: 1 Critical -- a fresh cold reviewer independently re-derived the worked trace, confirmed it correct as far as it went, then actively hunted for a new counter-example the same way the builder had, and found one: the gate only helps if SOME tick eventually reaches the pending instant; it does nothing if no tick on the entire tape ever does. Concrete counter-example: an anchor late in the session plus the tape's LAST trading day being a real early-close session (every bar at or before the funding instant's time-of-day) silently and permanently loses that day's contribution. Nothing in Revision 3's own Required Phase-0 matrix would have forced discovery of it. 2 Minor, 2 Nit also found and fixed

phase0_history.design: adds an unconditional end-of-tape flush (called once after ServeLoop.run() returns, bounded by the LAST scheduled funding instant rather than the last tick) that catches anything the per-tick gate structurally cannot reach; refactors the shared due()/append_many/balance/index logic into one _advance_cash_flow_window helper reused by both the per-tick gate and the flush
phase0_history.reason: root fix, not a narrower trigger condition -- addresses the general case (no tick anywhere on the tape reaches the instant) rather than the specific counter-example (an early-close last day)
phase0_history.review: third independent design skeptic, cold review, genuinely hunted for a fifth counter-example across six angles (empty funding_instants, off-by-one at the flush boundary, double-submission risk, instance-reuse safety, whether funding_instants itself could be structurally incomplete, interaction with the tick-loop's own exception handling) -- found none: 0 Critical, 0 Major, 2 Minor, 1 Nit, GO. All fixed in place before RED: the flush call wrapped in the same except-tuple -> ConfigError pattern evaluate()/quotes() already use; the shared helper's attribute sourcing stated explicitly rather than left implicit

reuse_confirmed.method: trading-day derivation is entirely internal to the replay's own tape data (no exchange-calendar library integration); the SkipCashFlow override mechanism, the composer.due() usage pattern, and the ledger/authorization machinery are all pre-existing, unedited ADR-0176 core -- this ADR only changes WHEN and under what filter EquityReplay calls into that existing surface
reuse_confirmed.action_taken: swept before drafting (documented in the ADR's Context section): confirmed no existing config/override/partial mechanism for calendar-aware timing existed anywhere in children/intraday_equities or dskit/production

two_sequential_clean_final_lenses.notes: independently re-verified every Decision point against git diff 52884e3 8ce1c73 (the diff since Phase-0 approval) rather than trusting the ADR's or commit message's claims: confirmed the single date-walk builds both SkipCashFlow overrides and funding_instants_ms with no duplication, confirmed the 2-tuple return and instance-reuse-safe resets in both branches, confirmed _advance_cash_flow_window is a genuine shared helper with success-only state advancement and a bounded index-advance loop, confirmed the flush target is the last funding instant not the last tick, confirmed no dskit/production/* file touched, confirmed backward-compatibility dead-code paths, confirmed the point-1.6 test asserts the funding index directly. 1 Minor: _flush_cash_flows's except-clause omits the self._fault stash evaluate()/quotes() use in their otherwise-identical pattern -- functionally inert (flush is called directly by _run_loop, not through ServeLoop's callback machinery that needs the fault stashed for later re-raise), no consequence demonstrated, accepted as a recorded Minor

active mutation testing specifically targeting the point-1.6 flush -- the highest-risk mechanism, having taken 3 revision rounds to design correctly -- with 5 mutations, all caught by name: removing the flush call entirely (4 tests failed, including the exact scenario it exists to close), an off-by-one at the flush boundary (caught by the funding_index assertion specifically, not masked by aggregate content), a boundary flip in the per-tick gate (5 tests failed, including the rewritten ADR-0176 boundary test), removing the no-op guard (9 tests failed, including a hard ConfigError from a backwards due() window), and inverting the skip/collect branch in composer_for (11 tests failed catastrophically, as expected). Confirmed no vacuous assertions, confirmed the scale test's call count and timing are reproducible across isolated re-runs (not boundary-adjacent), confirmed every test genuinely drives the real ServeLoop/HorizonBook/ledger machinery end-to-end via thin EquityReplay subclasses, never stubs

non_authority: This slice changes only the child-owned EquityReplay cash-flow timing mechanism (ADR-0176). No dskit/production module changed. No new capability, registry entry, or uses: site. No real market-calendar/exchange-calendar library integration (trading days are derived purely from the replay's own tape data). No redirect-to-next-trading-day behavior (an explicit owner decision against it). No change to the funding amount formula, the day-one $1,020 seed, or the ADR-0177 insufficient-cash mechanism. No ReplayRun/P4 wiring. No backtest launch, no paper/live trading, no deployment.
